title: Algebraic classification of Anosov diffeomorphisms
statement: Is every Anosov diffeomorphism of a closed manifold topologically conjugate to an affine Anosov map of an infranilmanifold?
status: As of November 2026, unresolved in general in the checked literature; see Spatzier’s Conjecture 2.3. The weaker manifold-realization question also remains open. The smooth-category replacement is too strong.

title: Structural stability of Morse--Smale systems
statement: Are Morse--Smale maps and flows \(C^1\) structurally stable?
status: Affirmatively solved; 1968 circulation, 1969 Russian and 1970 English publication.

title: Necessity of Morse--Smale conditions
statement: Must structural stability imply the Morse--Smale conditions?
status: No; hyperbolic toral automorphisms and their suspension flows provide counterexamples.

title: Density of Morse--Smale systems
statement: Are Morse--Smale systems dense on every closed manifold?
status: No in general; an open family of Anosov systems supplies an obstruction.

title: Density of structurally stable fields
statement: Are structurally stable vector fields dense on every compact manifold?
status: No in general, by Smale’s 1966 counterexample, already published at the time of the question.

title: Density of Axiom A
statement: Are Axiom A diffeomorphisms \(C^1\)-dense on every closed manifold?

title: Periodic density from hyperbolic nonwandering set
Uniqueness of the vanishing identity-viscosity limit
statement: Under what hypotheses do the solutions of \(u_t+A(u)u_x=\epsilon u_{xx}\) have a unique limit as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\)?
status: As of November 2026: Bianchini--Bressan solve the smooth strictly hyperbolic small-total-variation case. The notes do not determine a universal large-data conjecture.

title: Representative pair observables: moment hypotheses and concentration
statement: A precise question extracted from the representativeness argument is which moment and mixing hypotheses justify concentration of \(N^{-1}\sum_{i\ne j}f(x_i-x_j)\), and whether an arbitrary real even \(L^1\) kernel permits the claimed finite linear variance. Minlos’s later Problem 3 asks for quantitative inequalities in this argument. This entry does not index an unspecified all-density existence conjecture.
status: As of November 2026: the finite-variance claim under bare \(L^1\) is false even for an ideal gas. The chapter supplies a complete conditional correction with an explicit four-point bound, an \(L^1\) truncation conclusion, and counterexamples. These are checked critical annotations, not a claim that a previously open C/D problem has been solved. Establishing the assumed correlation bound in an interacting model remains model- and regime-dependent.
